why: Every command in both briefs would run as written. `npm test` maps to the existing script `node --test`. bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js and README.md are all tracked files. The verifier's pipelines, such as `printf 'name\tage...' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv > /tmp/tsv.out`, are valid shell, since printf turns \t into a tab. `cat`, `cmp /tmp/tsv.out /tmp/csv.out` and `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` (the `--` stops grep reading `--tsv` as an option) are also correct. The `--tsv` flag is added by the builder, so it exists at the PR head where the verifier runs. The JS the builder uses, `parse(input, '\t')`, matches `parse(text, sep = ',')`. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is only an example for the README text, not a command the agents are told to run. Step 4 tells the builder to run the commands on a small table, so it makes its own input file. No command breaks.
